newsitem.title: USA: Belarus diplomat leaves New York, officials say.
newsitem.headline: Belarus diplomat leaves New York, officials say.

text.p: A Belarus diplomat who was involved in a police fracas that led to a battle over parking between New York City authorities and the United Nations has left the United States, officials said on Tuesday.
A spokeswoman for the Belarus mission to the United Nations said the envoy, first secretary Yuri Orange, had left the country, but declined further comment.

Mayor Rudolph Giuliani fought to have the diplomat's immunity removed so he could be prosecuted for allegedly assaulting a police officer. On Tuesday, Giuliani did not go so far as to claim that his pressure led to Orange's departure but did his best to make that inference.

"It says to other diplomats that if they do the same kind of thing, if they try to drive drunk and assault police officers we'll do the same thing to them -- try to drive them out of this country and maybe that'll stop them from doing it," Giuliani told reporters.
The Dec. 29, 1996 incident involved Orange from Belarus and Boris Obnossov of Russia's U.N. mission.

Police said they pulled Obnossov from a car because he appeared intoxicated after parking illegally near a fire hydrant. Orange, who was travelling with Obnossov, was said to have punched one of the officers.
Giuliani started a campaign to remove the special license plates of diplomats who routinely ignore parking tickets, kicking off a dispute between the envoys and New York police and city officials.

The issue has still not been settled and Bill Richardson, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, has said hostility toward foreign diplomats was increasing in New York. He said police appeared to be harassing diplomats by deliberately targeting some of them in issuing parking fines.
On June 5, the U.S. State Department said it had asked Russia and Belarus to lift the immunity of the two diplomats involved in the fracas with New York police.
